changelog.note: The owner's decisions of 2026-11-02 (the framework works without the legacy project; Azure reads at most max_pages pages): the Docker engine (the legacy sidecar's image) and the sidecar route (sidecar_url, container_root) removed, Azure is called only directly with this installation's own endpoint and key; azure_di.retries and retry_max_wait_s (a start refused for load is repeated), max_file_mb (the service's 500 MB, checked before sending), check_timeout_s (the free check of the endpoint and key) and poll_interval_s 2.0 (the service's advice). The OCR cache key loses the docker section: `python -m jav.cli ocr-rekey --from-rev v1.79.1` moves every native and Azure text to the new key with no new OCR.

tesseract.language_packs: where a fresh installation gets the native recogniser's language packs (python -m jav.cli ocr --fetch-langs) and the SHA-256 of each file; they are the files already in use, so no value that changes the recognised text moves and the cache key is unchanged.
The notes and the description without the development process's references; no value changes.

Azure DI is called directly over its REST API when AZURE_DI_ENDPOINT and AZURE_DI_KEY are set (jav/adapters/azure_di.py; azure_di.api_version, azure_di.poll_interval_s); the legacy sidecar route stays for a machine without them. Before this, every document outside the legacy data folder failed before the network. An escalation that cannot run (no route, a failed call, an unknown outcome) now raises a to-do when the recipe's Azure switch is on. The cache key is unchanged: the new settings are not output settings, and the API version is the one every earlier Azure text was read with.

The OCR chain: a PDF without text -> page images (pypdfium2, 300 dpi, grey) -> tesseract word boxes (TSV) -> the same line and cell builder as for a PDF with a text layer (jav/pdf.py). Engine: the native tesseract (5.4 installed on the machine, the Hungarian and English language data from the legacy sidecar's Docker image, tools/tessdata); fallback: the legacy sidecar image (aiflow-v4-sidecar) with docker run when there is no native one. The legacy sidecar's settings: hun+eng, 200 dpi -> 300 dpi here (for the small numbers of the bill's itemisation), psm 3 (automatic page segmentation). A disk cache in runs/ocr/ (the document's sha256, the config hash and the tesseract version in the key).

Azure_di.data_root removed; the sidecar's /data mount is the legacy project's data folder (JAV_LEGACY_ROOT, jav/config.py). The OCR cache key now covers only the settings that can change the recognised text (jav/ocr.py output_settings), so paths, time limits, notes and this version record do not invalidate it; the existing cache was moved to the new key once (python -m jav.cli ocr-rekey), with no new OCR.

escalation.note: The owner's decision (2026-09-20): tesseract by default, Azure DI only on weak OCR; the thresholds (mean word confidence, share of weak words) are in policy.json ocr.escalate_*; instead of the weak local OCR the Azure text goes on, and both stay in the cache

language_packs.note: The tesseract-ocr project's tessdata_fast release 4.1.0: byte for byte the files the legacy sidecar's image held and every measurement read with. `python -m jav.cli ocr --fetch-langs` puts the missing ones into tessdata_dir and keeps a file only when its SHA-256 matches; a different file already there is left alone and reported.

azure_di.note: Azure Document Intelligence (prebuilt-read; the model and its price per page are in models.json), PAID and priced per page; never 'auto': only escalation, engine = azure_di or JAV_OCR_ENGINE=azure_di. Called only directly over the REST API, with AZURE_DI_ENDPOINT and AZURE_DI_KEY from this installation's .env (jav/documents/azure_di.py); without them it is not set up here and a weak scan keeps its local text with a to-do. At most max_pages pages are analysed and billed (the `pages` range). timeout_s bounds the whole call, repeats and polling included; a start the service refuses for load (429, 5xx) is repeated at most `retries` times, waiting as it asks, at most retry_max_wait_s. A changed api_version gives the Azure texts a new cache key (jav/documents/ocr.py engine_version); none of the other settings here change what is read.
